item.content:encoded: A Molino resident was sentenced to a year of community control and probation after pleading no contest to felony battery for punching a man outside a Pensacola bar and breaking his jaw. Travis Keith Hethington, 28, reached the plea agreement with prosecutors following the January altercation. The sentencing comes after the incident left the victim with significant facial injuries requiring treatment. Hethington's sentence emphasizes supervised release rather than incarceration, meaning he'll remain in the community under strict conditions while serving out his punishment.

item.content:encoded: Escambia County residents planning outdoor Labor Day activities should prepare for afternoon and evening storms. According to the National Weather Service forecast for North Escambia, showers and thunderstorms are likely to develop between 1 p.m. and 4 p.m., with additional storm chances continuing after 4 p.m. The high is expected to reach the low 90s with calm winds. Forecasters put the chance of precipitation at 60%, so those heading to the beach, parks, or hosting cookouts should keep an eye on the sky and have a backup plan. Monday morning should start with sunny skies before conditions deteriorate in the afternoon.

item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos punched their ticket to the postseason Tuesday night with a dramatic ninth-inning rally, capping off a season that tested the team's resilience at nearly every turn.

The minor league squad fought back late in the game to secure the win and the playoff berth, delivering the kind of clutch performance that defines October baseball. It's a fitting exclamation point on what has been a challenging year for the Double-A affiliate.

"This team showed tremendous heart all season," the Blue Wahoos said in a statement. "We knew we had to fight for every win, and this one proves why we belong in the playoffs."

The Blue Wahoos will now prepare for postseason play as they look to build on their late-season momentum. Fans can expect more details about playoff matchups and schedules in the coming days.

item.title: Florida's Hunting, Fishing Tax Holiday Runs Through Year-End
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida's four-month sales tax holiday for outdoor enthusiasts is now in effect through December 31, offering shoppers tax breaks on a wide range of gear and equipment. The holiday covers hunting, fishing, and camping items with varying price limits. Shoppers can save on tents, fishing rods, and other traditional outdoor gear — though individual…
item.content:encoded:
Florida's four-month sales tax holiday for outdoor enthusiasts is now in effect through December 31, offering shoppers tax breaks on a wide range of gear and equipment.

The holiday covers hunting, fishing, and camping items with varying price limits. Shoppers can save on tents, fishing rods, and other traditional outdoor gear — though individual items are subject to price caps. Firearms and tactical accessories, however, have no price limitations, meaning the full sales tax exemption applies regardless of cost.

The break applies to both in-store and online purchases from Florida retailers. For Escambia County and surrounding areas with significant hunting and fishing traditions, the holiday provides savings during the peak season for outdoor recreation. Shoppers interested in stocking up on gear before the holidays or planning winter hunting and fishing trips have about six weeks to take advantage of the tax savings.

More details about specific price limits and qualifying items are available through the Florida Department of Revenue.

item.title: Gas prices up 80 cents ahead of Labor Day weekend across Florida
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida drivers heading into the Labor Day holiday are facing significantly higher fuel costs compared to last year, according to AAA data. The average price per gallon across the state hit $3.91 on Sunday night, marking an 80-cent jump from the $3.11 average a year ago. While prices ticked up just two cents from the previous week, the…
item.content:encoded:
Florida drivers heading into the Labor Day holiday are facing significantly higher fuel costs compared to last year, according to AAA data. The average price per gallon across the state hit $3.91 on Sunday night, marking an 80-cent jump from the $3.11 average a year ago.

While prices ticked up just two cents from the previous week, the year-over-year increase reflects broader trends in fuel costs that have persisted throughout 2024. The timing coincides with one of the busiest travel weekends of the summer season, when many Northwest Florida residents take to the roads for Labor Day trips.

AAA tracks gas prices daily and provides real-time updates for drivers planning their travel budgets. For Pensacola-area motorists heading out for the holiday weekend, the current price point represents a notable difference from last year's Labor Day period.

item.content:encoded:

Michael Earl Beasley was wanted in connection with an Aug. 20 incident at the motel located on the 3100 block of Dr. Martin Luther King Drive. He faces charges of attempted homicide and burglary in the case.

The Escambia County Sheriff's Office apprehended Beasley on the warrant charges. Additional details about the circumstances of the stabbing were not immediately available.

item.content:encoded:
A correctional officer at Century Correctional Institution was assaulted by an inmate this week, according to the Florida Department of Corrections. Inmate Dwayne A. Collins grabbed the officer during the incident, but no staff members were injured in the altercation.

Collins is serving a 30-year sentence for a 2013 homicide conviction out of Highlands County. The circumstances surrounding the assault and any disciplinary action against the inmate have not been detailed by the FDC.

Century Correctional Institution, located in North Escambia County, houses adult male inmates and is part of Florida's state prison system.

The shooting happened near the intersection of King Street and Sims Street in Atmore. Details about the victim's condition were not immediately available, nor did police provide information about potential suspects.

Atmore Police have not yet released additional details about the investigation. Anyone with information about the incident is encouraged to contact the Atmore Police Department.

The lopsided victory caps a dominant stretch for the Argos, who entered the contest ranked No. 25 in one major poll and are likely to climb both national rankings…
item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida football team delivered another impressive statement in its Division I transition, dismantling No. 24 Central Arkansas 42-14 on the road Saturday night. The lopsided victory caps a dominant stretch for the Argos, who entered the contest ranked No. 25 in one major poll and are likely to climb both national rankings following the convincing performance.

According to reporting on the game, UWF's complete control on both sides of the ball against a ranked opponent suggests the young Division I program is moving faster up the competitive ladder than many expected. The road win—always tougher than home games—demonstrates the Argos can execute at a high level away from Pensacola.

The emphatic victory adds to the momentum surrounding UWF's historic jump to the FCS level. With several weeks of the season remaining, the Argos appear positioned to compete for bowl eligibility in their debut Division I campaign.

Blacklidge's employment status with the Department of Homeland Security and any potential federal involvement in the case remain unclear. The Baldwin County case will likely draw scrutiny given the defendant's federal law enforcement background.

item.title: Wahoos Edge Clingstones 8-6 in 10 Innings, Magic Number Down to 3
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Blue Wahoos stayed hot Friday night, grinding out an extra-inning victory over the Columbus Clingstones that keeps them firmly in control of their division race. After a tight pitching contest through nine innings, the Wahoos broke through in the 10th to win 8-6. The victory extends Pensacola's lead over Columbus to 5.5 games with…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos stayed hot Friday night, grinding out an extra-inning victory over the Columbus Clingstones that keeps them firmly in control of their division race.

After a tight pitching contest through nine innings, the Wahoos broke through in the 10th to win 8-6. The victory extends Pensacola's lead over Columbus to 5.5 games with just eight regular-season games remaining.

With the win, the Wahoos' magic number—the number of wins they need combined with Columbus losses to clinch the division—dropped to 3. The team is positioned well heading into the final stretch of the season, according to reporting from North Escambia.

The Wahoos will look to keep the momentum rolling as they push toward the postseason.

item.title: Escambia Gators Hold Off Tate for First Win of Season
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia High School Gators got off the shutout streak Friday night, edging the previously unbeaten Tate Aggies 6-3 in a defensive struggle that gave coach Mike Bennett his first victory of the season. Escambia had dropped its first two games without scoring before finding the end zone against Tate. The Gators' defensive effort kept the…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia High School Gators got off the shutout streak Friday night, edging the previously unbeaten Tate Aggies 6-3 in a defensive struggle that gave coach Mike Bennett his first victory of the season.

Escambia had dropped its first two games without scoring before finding the end zone against Tate. The Gators' defensive effort kept the Aggies' high-powered offense in check, limiting them to just a field goal in what turned into a low-scoring affair.

Tate, under coach Rhett Summerford, came in undefeated and looking to stay perfect through three weeks of play. The Aggies' offense, which had been prolific early in the season, couldn't find its rhythm against Escambia's defense on Friday.

The win marks a turning point for the Gators program as they look to build momentum heading into the rest of their schedule.

item.title: Hot, humid Labor Day weekend ahead with afternoon storm chance
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Plan for typical late-summer weather this Labor Day weekend across North Escambia, with highs climbing near 90 degrees and a solid chance of afternoon thunderstorms Saturday. According to the National Weather Service forecast, Saturday will bring a 50 percent chance of showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon hours, with mostly sunny skies…
item.content:encoded:
Plan for typical late-summer weather this Labor Day weekend across North Escambia, with highs climbing near 90 degrees and a solid chance of afternoon thunderstorms Saturday.

According to the National Weather Service forecast, Saturday will bring a 50 percent chance of showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon hours, with mostly sunny skies otherwise. Winds will remain calm throughout the day. If storms develop, rainfall could reach a quarter-inch or more in isolated areas, though most spots will see a tenth to quarter-inch of moisture.

Saturday night conditions improve slightly, with only a 20 percent chance of showers after 1 a.m. Those planning outdoor Labor Day activities should keep an eye on afternoon storm development but shouldn't expect significant weather disruptions overall.

Few additional details have been released about the nature of the confrontation or what led to the incident. The sheriff's office is continuing its investigation into the circumstances surrounding the armed disturbance. Anyone with information about what happened is encouraged to contact the Escambia County Sheriff's Office.

item.title: Pensacola Worship Leader Battles Terminal Brain Cancer With Faith and Music
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Toby Moore, a worship leader and frontman for a Christian rock band based in Pensacola, is channeling his faith and passion for music as he navigates a diagnosis of terminal brain cancer. According to WKRG News 5, Moore has become an inspiration to those around him by maintaining his focus on serving others despite the serious health challenge he…
item.content:encoded:
Toby Moore, a worship leader and frontman for a Christian rock band based in Pensacola, is channeling his faith and passion for music as he navigates a diagnosis of terminal brain cancer. According to WKRG News 5, Moore has become an inspiration to those around him by maintaining his focus on serving others despite the serious health challenge he faces.

Moore's journey illustrates how some people in our community are finding meaning and purpose during life's most difficult moments. Rather than withdrawing from his calling, he continues his work leading worship and creating music—activities that have become central to how he processes his diagnosis and connects with his faith.

The Pensacola worship leader's story reflects the resilience of local faith communities and the role that music and spirituality play in helping individuals cope with profound adversity. WKRG's reporting highlights Moore's determination to maintain his ministry and relationships even as he manages the physical and emotional toll of terminal illness.
